# Hand-authored mechanisms for concepts previously used mainly as targets.
# Definitions are not generated by reversing arbitrary scientific implications.
# Capillarity is a phenomenon; capillary is also the name of a blood vessel.
adhesion | attraction different molecules surfaces
cohesion | attraction identical molecules
adhesion water glass | wetting spread meniscus
cohesion water | hydrogen bonds droplets surface tension
surface tension | cohesive forces liquid surface
surface tension detergent | decrease disrupted cohesion
capillarity | liquid movement narrow tubes adhesion cohesion
capillarity cause | adhesion cohesion surface tension
capillary action | liquid movement narrow tube adhesion cohesion surface tension
water capillarity narrow tube | higher rise
water capillarity | upward rise narrow tube
mercury capillarity | depression lower level
water meniscus glass | concave adhesion
mercury meniscus glass | convex cohesion
paper towel wicking | capillarity adhesion absorption
capillary blood | thin walls exchange oxygen nutrients
# Tropisms describe directional growth, not necessarily attraction to a cue.
tropism | directional plant growth stimulus
gravitropism | growth response gravity
hydrotropism | growth response water moisture
thigmotropism | growth response touch contact
positive tropism | toward stimulus | away | -1.0
negative tropism | away stimulus | toward | -1.0
toward stimulus growth | positive tropism
away stimulus growth | negative tropism
positive phototropism | toward light | away | -1.0
negative phototropism | away light | toward | -1.0
positive gravitropism | downward gravity root | upward | -1.0
negative gravitropism | upward shoot stem | downward | -1.0
root gravitropism | positive downward
shoot gravitropism | negative upward
root hydrotropism | toward moist soil
stem phototropism | light bending auxin
auxin | plant hormone growth cell elongation
shoot shaded side | auxin elongation bending light
vine touch | thigmotropism tendril coil
tendril support | touch growth coiling climbing
# Growth and respiratory structures in insects and other arthropods.
molt | shed outer covering growth
arthropod molting | shed exoskeleton growth larger
exoskeleton | external rigid covering support protection
arthropod exoskeleton | chitin external support protection
insect molting growth | rigid exoskeleton replaced larger
new exoskeleton | soft vulnerable hardens
nymph | immature insect resembles adult incomplete metamorphosis
nymph development | molting growth adult | pupa
grasshopper lifecycle | egg nymph adult incomplete
spiracle | external opening insect gas exchange
insect trachea | air tubes oxygen directly tissues
spiracle function | air enters trachea respiration
insect respiration | spiracles trachea diffusion
insect spiracle closing | conserve water reduce evaporation
